sources.name: LA County DPH Environmental Health - Restaurant and Market Inventory (ArcGIS Hub)
sources.contains: Inventory of all active food facilities (restaurants and markets) permitted by LA County Environmental Health. Fields confirmed via hub.arcgis.com/api/v3/datasets/4f31c9a99e444a40a3806e3bbe7b5fdd: FACILITY ID, FACILITY NAME, PROGRAM NAME, PROGRAM ELEMENT, PE DESCRIPTION (facility type / seat-count / risk class), FACILITY ADDRESS, FACILITY CITY, FACILITY STATE, FACILITY ZIP, FACILITY LATITUDE, FACILITY LONGITUDE, OWNER ID/NAME/ADDRESS. Coverage: unincorporated LA County plus 85 of 88 cities (excludes Pasadena, Long Beach, Vernon) - so City of LA (DTLA, Koreatown) is included. Updated quarterly. Has lat/long, so radius counts around 768 Ceres Ave are possible. Record count not shown in the metadata I retrieved; must download to count. No neighborhood field - needs spatial join to neighborhood polygons.
sources.year: snapshot titled 07/01/2026 in API (search listing showed a 04/01/2026 edition; metadata 'last item modified' 2025-01-01)
headline_datapoints: Dataset title: 'Environmental Health Restaurant and Market Inventory 07/01/2026' (quarterly snapshot)
Fields include FACILITY LATITUDE and FACILITY LONGITUDE and PE DESCRIPTION (facility type)
Coverage: unincorporated areas + 85 of 88 cities in LA County (excludes Pasadena, Long Beach, Vernon)

Not opened; fields not confirmed (likely same facility/PE fields as inventory). Search snippet notes inspection REPORTS conducted on or after 2025-08-25 must now be requested via CPRA, so the open inspections dataset may be truncated after that date.

sources.name: LA County DPH Environmental Health - View Inspection Results (facility lookup)
sources.contains: Per-facility search UI for grades/inspections; not a bulk dataset. Useful only for spot checks.

sources.name: City of LA Open Data - Restaurant and Market Health Inspections (Socrata 29fd-3paw)
sources.contains: City-of-LA subset of county inspections. Confirmed via https://data.lacity.org/api/views/29fd-3paw.json: 20 columns incl. facility_name, facility_address, facility_city, facility_zip, pe_description (30 facility types by seat count / risk), program_element_pe (codes 1610-1641), score, grade, program_status. NO latitude/longitude column. STALE: rowsUpdatedAt = 2018-09-10.
headline_datapoints: pe_description has 30 facility-type categories; program_element_pe codes 1610-1641

sources.name: City of LA Office of Finance - Listing of Active Businesses (Socrata 6rrh-rzua)
sources.contains: All active businesses registered with LA Office of Finance (City of LA only). Confirmed columns: location_account, business_name, dba_name, street_address, city, zip_code, location_description, mailing fields, naics (2007 NAICS), primary_naics_description, council_district, location_start_date, location_end_date, location_1 (lat/long location type). Computed regions: zip codes, council districts, census tracts, precincts, specific plans, neighborhood councils. Updated monthly. Allows NAICS 722 (food services) filtering and radius counts around 768 Ceres; also non-restaurant merchant density (grocery, pharmacy). Caveat: NAICS self-reported at registration, coordinates completeness not verified.
sources.granularity: business-location-level point data with NAICS, City of LA only
headline_datapoints: rowsUpdatedAt 2026-06-04; has location_1 (lat/long) and naics + primary_naics_description columns
Computed region: neighborhood councils (e.g., Wilshire Center-Koreatown NC, Downtown LA NC) usable as neighborhood proxy

sources.name: SF DPH - Health Inspection Scores (2024-Present) (Socrata tvy3-wexg)
sources.contains: Current SF DPH food facility inspections 2024 onward. Confirmed columns: inspection_date, district, subdistrict, subsector, permit_number, dba, permit_type (facility type), street_address, inspection_type, facility_rating_status (Pass / Conditional Pass / Closure), violation_count, violation_codes, latitude, longitude, point, analysis_neighborhood, supervisor_district, data_as_of. Dedupe on permit_number to get active facility counts by Analysis Neighborhood (South of Market, Mission, Tenderloin, Financial District/South Beach).
sources.granularity: inspection-level with facility lat/long and Analysis Neighborhood
headline_datapoints: rowsUpdatedAt 2026-09-06; includes latitude, longitude, point, analysis_neighborhood, permit_type

gaps: No public source gives delivery ORDER volume or platform merchant counts by LA neighborhood; restaurant density is a proxy that still needs an orders-per-restaurant and deliveries-per-courier conversion from other modalities.

LA County inventory record count and the share of rows with valid lat/long are unconfirmed; the dataset must be downloaded to count facilities within 1/2/3 miles of 768 Ceres Ave and inside DTLA/Koreatown polygons.

LA datasets carry no neighborhood field; DTLA vs Koreatown vs Westlake counts require a spatial join to neighborhood boundaries (e.g., LA Times Mapping L.A. polygons or LA City neighborhood-council boundaries) - boundaries not retrieved in this pass.
No authoritative Koreatown or DTLA restaurant totals found; the '700+ restaurants / 2.7 sq mi' Koreatown figure comes from a travel guide and is unverified.
LA County inspection REPORTS on/after 2025-08-25 now require a CPRA request; freshness of the open inspections dataset after that date is unverified (inventory snapshot still appears quarterly).

Ghost kitchens / virtual brands (a large DTLA/Koreatown delivery supply source) cannot be distinguished from dine-in restaurants in either county inventory or business-license data without manual tagging by PE description or address clustering.

SF and LA facility taxonomies differ (SF permit_type vs LA PE DESCRIPTION), so like-for-like SF-vs-LA counts need a harmonized definition (e.g., NAICS 7225 in both business-license datasets as the cleaner comparison).
Uber Eats / DoorDash neighborhood merchant pages exist but only via scraping; no press release with LA neighborhood-level merchant or order counts was found in this pass.
must_ask_hmp: Geocoded (or zip-level) home and primary-work locations for the ~1,000 SF buyers, ~300 battery renters and ~100 vehicle renters, so the SF core-zone restaurant count can be converted into an observed customers-per-restaurant ratio for task 2.
Which SF neighborhoods customers actually deliver in (their platform zone / hotspot), distinct from where they live, to define the SF comparison polygon correctly.
Self-reported platform mix (DoorDash / Uber Eats / Grubhub) and average deliveries per shift among SF customers, to anchor the restaurants-to-riders conversion.
Any existing LA-area orders, inquiries or leads by zip code (web store ship-to, Instagram DMs) as an independent early demand signal for DTLA/Koreatown.
Whether HMP already has courier-community contacts (WhatsApp/KakaoTalk groups) in Koreatown who could provide platform screenshots of merchant density / order heat maps.
surprises: LA County's open data portal (data.lacounty.gov) is now ArcGIS Hub, not Socrata; the Socrata-style https://data.lacounty.gov/api/views/<id>.json endpoint suggested in the brief does not apply - use https://hub.arcgis.com/api/v3/datasets/<id> instead. The City of LA Socrata mirror of inspections (29fd-3paw) has been dead since 2018-09-10 and has no coordinates.

LA County DPH has restricted inspection reports dated on/after 2025-08-25 to CPRA requests, so the county inspection dataset is less current than expected; the quarterly facility INVENTORY (with lat/long) is the usable density source instead.

SF's well-known LIVES inspections dataset (pyih-qa8i) stopped in 2019; a successor dataset (tvy3-wexg, 2024-present, rows updated 2026-09-06) exists with lat/long and analysis_neighborhood, and switched from numeric scores to Pass/Conditional Pass/Closure.

Both cities have current, monthly-or-better business-license datasets with NAICS and coordinates (LA 6rrh-rzua updated 2026-06-04; SF g8m3-pdis updated 2026-09-06), giving a cleaner apples-to-apples restaurant-density method than health inspections.
